symptom: In two disposable Linux tests, openat2 RESOLVE_BENEATH|RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS rejected ancestor symlink and root escape while a pinned root FD still resolved a substituted real intermediate directory to decoy JSON; a pre-pinned vault FD retained original bytes. Adding RESOLVE_NO_XDEV rejected an existing /proc mount crossing without mounting anything. Both tests passed official CI. This is not a live SDK exploit or production incident.
lesson: On supported Linux, openat2 resolver flags constrain all-component symlinks, escapes and existing mount traversal. A trusted root FD with those flags does not bind a later lookup to a previously observed real intermediate directory object: rename-and-replacement can redirect it. A pre-pinned final directory FD preserves object-relative readback, but canonical reachability remains separate.
guardrail: Reuse RESOLVE_BENEATH|RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS and security-justified RESOLVE_NO_XDEV as bounded traversal constraints only, never as proof of publisher identity or canonical reachability. Pin and independently authenticate the common reader/writer directory object; account for EAGAIN under concurrent rename, unsupported kernels, bind mounts and power loss before any native integration. Never auto-delete by stale path, weaken strict SDK readback, activate N2, connect BUY or infer merge/production authority.
